content.title: About
content.content: Orange bell pepper (Capsicum annuum) is a mature fruit of the sweet pepper plant, consumed raw. It has a bright color, sweet slightly fruity flavor and a crunchy texture. The pepper is rich in vitamins, especially vitamin C, and is used in salads, snacks and as a garnish.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The orange color appears when the pepper fully ripens, increasing its sugar content.
Sweet peppers belong to the nightshade family and are relatives of chili peppers, but contain negligible capsaicin.
Peppers were first domesticated in Central and South America over 6,000 years ago.
Orange peppers are often used to add visual appeal to dishes without adding heat.
Vitamin C content in orange pepper exceeds that of oranges.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C is a powerful antioxidant that supports the immune system and aids collagen synthesis.

items.title: Contains vitamin A and carotenoids
items.content: Carotenoids such as beta‑carotene are important for vision and skin health.

items.title: Low‑calorie source of fiber
items.content: Fiber promotes digestive health and helps maintain a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Source of potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate blood pressure and supports muscle function.

items.title: Provides folate
items.content: Folate is essential for DNA synthesis and is especially beneficial during pregnancy.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to pepper, manifested as skin rash or swelling.

items.title: Foodborne contamination
items.content: If stored at high temperatures, peppers can develop mold or bacteria that cause food poisoning.

items.title: Digestive discomfort
items.content: Large amounts of raw pepper may cause gas and discomfort in people with sensitive stomachs.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Orange bell pepper can be eaten raw in salads, sliced into strips for snacks, added to sandwiches and smoothies. It can also be lightly sautéed, though this reduces some vitamin C.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store peppers in the refrigerator’s vegetable drawer, in a plastic bag or container. When kept properly, they stay fresh for 1‑2 weeks. Discard any peppers showing signs of rot or softness.
